title: Winterspring
body: Winterspring is a high valley of snow and ice in the mountains of northern Kalimdor, east of Felwood, north of Azshara and northeast of Mount Hyjal. Most travelers reach it through the tunnels of Timbermaw Hold. Long ago the night elves raised the city of Kel'Theril here, and beside its ruins the cursed spirits of Highborne still drift over a frozen lake. In the Third War Tyrande Whisperwind and Malfurion Stormrage fought across these snows and woke the Druids of the Talon from their barrow dens. Today the goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel keep the trading post of Everlook at the crossroads of the valley, and night elves hold Starfall Village to its northwest. Frostsabers prowl the northern heights, maddened wildkin guard old sacred places, and the Winterfall furbolgs have turned savage. Blue dragons lair in the caverns of Mazthoril, frost giants hold a canyon in the south, and beyond it, in Darkwhisper Gorge, demons stand between the valley and the heights of Hyjal.

title: Frostfire Hot Springs
body: At the far western end of Winterspring, close to the mouth of Timbermaw Hold, steaming pools break through the snow. No volcano lies anywhere near them, and that riddle has drawn the dwarf Donova Snowden, who keeps watch beside one of the springs and has found that their water has strange qualities. She suspects a darker cause than fire beneath the earth: the demons of Darkwhisper Gorge, far to the south, whose presence she believes is warming the land. The Winterfall furbolgs are drawn to the springs as well. Their pathfinders and den watchers guard the two larger pools fiercely and drive off anyone who comes near.

title: Timbermaw Post
body: Southeast of the road that runs from the hot springs toward the heart of Winterspring lies Timbermaw Post, a small furbolg camp. Its name suggests that the Timbermaw of the nearby hold once kept it, but the camp now belongs wholly to the Winterfall tribe, whose den watchers and pathfinders stand guard there while owlbeasts and shardtooth bears roam the slopes around it. Salfa, who guards the Winterspring gate of the hold, remembers that the Winterfall were once allies of the Timbermaw, until the strange demands of a high chief turned them against everyone they met.

title: Lake Kel'Theril
body: In the center of Winterspring lies Lake Kel'Theril, frozen hard beneath the mountain wind. Long ago Highborne sorcerers stole a sacred relic, the Crystal of Zin-Malor, from a temple in Eldarath, hoping to siphon its power and become greater still. Their ritual failed. The crystal shattered in a tremendous explosion, and its pieces were driven deep beneath the ice of the lake. The thieves were cursed to remain where they had worked their folly, and their suffering, anguished spirits still drift over the frozen water, searching for fragments of the very thing that doomed them. Chimaerae, bears and owlbeasts hunt along the shore.

title: The Ruins of Kel'Theril
body: On the shore of Lake Kel'Theril lie the remains of a great Highborne city, broken in the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago. Among its fallen stones walk the spirits of the Highborne who died here, suffering and anguished, still bound by the curse of the crystal their people stole. Nearly all of them are lost in their own misery and cannot be reached. One alone, a remorseful spirit, has come to understand the error of what was done so long ago, though it knows the past cannot be undone. The night elf Ranshalla has studied the carvings on these stones and believes they hold the incantations of an ancient altar of Elune.

title: Starfall Village
body: Starfall Village is a small night elf settlement on the main road between Everlook and Frostsaber Rock, and the only Alliance outpost in Winterspring. A lodge and a smaller house shelter sellers of food, goods and trade supplies, and the village keeps the old Ban'Thallow Barrow Den. Wynd Nightchaser spends most of his days here and knows a great deal about the valley and its secrets. A dwarf has come as well, Jaron Stoneshaper of the Explorers' League, who hunts the magical artifacts said to lie in Winterspring, most of them fiercely guarded. He rests here now, after the wildkin chased him from his camp.

title: Frostsaber Rock
body: In the far north of Winterspring a great tor juts above the snow, and around it gather the frostsabers, the most feral and hardest to tame of all the great cats. Their matriarch is Shy-Rotam, whose stone stands among the pride. About four thousand years ago Tyrande Whisperwind saved the frostsaber queen from rampaging giants, and since that day the cats have been allies of the night elves. Huntresses, stalkers and pride watchers roam among the cubs, and a great cat called Rak'shiri hunts among them. At the top of the rock the night elf Rivern Frostwind and his companion Glacier patiently train frostsabers to carry riders.

title: Everlook
body: Everlook is a trading post of the Steamwheedle Cartel, built where the main trade routes of Winterspring meet. Like the Cartel's other towns it is neutral ground, and its goblin bruisers have no patience for anyone who spills blood within its walls. An inn, a market and the only bank in the valley serve travelers of every race. The town draws curious company: Gregor Greystone speaks for the Argent Dawn before the local governance, Malyfous Darkhammer represents the Thorium Brotherhood, a troll witch doctor makes lucky charms, and a stern tauren sets trials for the bold.

title: Mazthoril
body: Mazthoril is a deep cavern of ice in central Winterspring, near Lake Kel'Theril and Everlook, and the home of the blue dragonflight in these lands. Cobalt wyrmkin, scalebanes and mageweavers guard its frozen halls among whelps, broodlings and spell eaters, while the drakes Spellmaw, Manaclaw and Scryer keep watch and the blue General Colbatann stalks its passages. At the heart of it all dwells Haleh, the matron protectorate of the flight. Her chamber at the cavern's peak is reached only by magic: cobalt runes set into the icy floor carry those who hold one of the flight's scales up to her.

title: Ice Thistle Hills
body: Southeast of Everlook rise the Ice Thistle Hills, the country of the Ice Thistle yeti. They make their home in a cave high in the hills and roam the snowy slopes around it, and their great patriarchs and matriarchs carry the largest horns of their kind. Chillwind chimaerae and shardtooth bears hunt the same ground. The yeti know little peace, for their thick fur and pristine horns are prized in Everlook, where Umi Rumplesnicker once needed both to build a mechanical yeti of her own. A blue dragon named Azurous roams the hills as well.

title: Winterfall Village
body: Far to the east lies Winterfall Village, the home of the Winterfall furbolgs. The tribe was never known for aggression, yet its ursa, shamans and den watchers now fall upon nearly anything that comes near. The change began with the strange demands of High Chief Winterfall, who keeps to the mouth of a cave at the edge of the village and carries a crude log that no one can easily read. His people drink a glowing firewater brewed from corrupted ooze, and the Timbermaw came to learn that a demon named Xandivious lurked behind their madness. The fierce Grizzle Snowpaw prowls the camp, and yeti and shardtooth bears roam nearby.

title: The Hidden Grove
body: In the northeast of Winterspring a forested crater lies hidden behind high cliffs on every side. The only ordinary way in is a cave in the southeastern face of the ridge, though a bold climber might risk the drop from the cliffs above. Within lies a haunt of moontouched owlbeasts, the hostile wildkin of the northern valley, which are fiercer than their kin elsewhere in Winterspring. A few crazed and berserk owlbeasts live among them, and more of their moontouched kind roam the snowy ground beyond the cliffs.

title: Owl Wing Thicket
body: Owl Wing Thicket is a series of caves along a ridge in southern Winterspring, overrun by crazed, berserk and moontouched owlbeasts. Horde runners report that these wildkin seem to have gone mad from exposure to the very thing they guard. At the top of the ridge lies an ancient altar of the goddess Elune, sealed until torches in the caves are lit and old incantations spoken over it. At the foot of the ridge waits the night elf Ranshalla, a colleague of the scholar Erelas Ambersky, fresh from studying the Ruins of Kel'Theril and determined to learn why the wildkin defend this place so fiercely.

title: Dun Mandarr
body: Dun Mandarr is a small camp beside an icy cavern in southeastern Winterspring, set up by the dwarf Jaron Stoneshaper of the Explorers' League. It did not last. Soon after Jaron unearthed a blue-feathered amulet at his dig site, bloodthirsty wildkin fell upon the camp, smashing his crates and wagon and chasing him away, and he fears a friend of his was not so lucky. Owlbeasts and screeching owls now haunt the wreckage, and what remains of his tools lies half buried in the snow. The beasts seemed to want the amulet above all else, and Jaron still wonders why they defended it so fiercely.

title: Frostwhisper Gorge
body: Frostwhisper Gorge is a deep canyon in the south of Winterspring, held by the frostmaul giants, great beings of solid ice. Shards of ice litter its floor, reflective enough to catch the light like mirrors and prized by those who make charms. These are the same giants from whom Tyrande Whisperwind once saved the frostsaber queen, and Rivern Frostwind still asks friends of the frostsabers to strike them down in Shy-Rotam's name. A brute called Kashoch the Reaver walks among them. Night elf ruins lie along the ridges, where a satyr named Lorax paces in an old temple, and a great bridge spans the chasm toward Darkwhisper Gorge.

title: Darkwhisper Gorge
body: In the far south of Winterspring the air turns thick and muggy and the sky grows dark. This is Darkwhisper Gorge, a maze of tunnels and chasms where demons have made their home, led by Lady Hederine and her manastalkers, slayers and initiates. Donova Snowden believes their presence is what heats the springs far to the north. The demons are not the gorge's only odd residents. An imp named Vi'el keeps a shop of exotic reagents in a cave, and seems startled when a customer slips past the minion at his door, and at the bottom of the gorge the high elf Earthcaller Franzahl studies the elements. Deeper still, a runed gateway faces toward Mount Hyjal, sealed and silent.

title: Donova Snowden
body: Donova Snowden is a dwarf who came to Winterspring to study the Frostfire Hot Springs and has stayed beside them a long while since. Cold, vast and dismal as the valley may seem, she calls it a place of many secrets. Her friend Krakle of Un'Goro sends curious travelers her way, for these springs steam with no volcano anywhere near. Donova has found that things thrown into the water come out greatly improved, a gift she once put to use on a forgetful gnome's sword. She suspects the heat rises from the demons of Darkwhisper Gorge, and a sudden bad feeling can set her glancing nervously over her shoulder.

title: Haleh
body: Haleh is the matron protectorate of the blue dragonflight, a consort of Malygos who dwells at the peak of Mazthoril and receives visitors in the guise of a high elf. The Aspects insist that dragons stay out of mortal affairs, yet Haleh will not stand idle while one of their own kind scorns that law. Nefarian, of the cursed brood of Deathwing, schemes behind the protection of Blackrock Mountain toward ends the blue flight cannot allow. Because the mountain makes it ever harder for the flight to intercede, Haleh offers her power to mortals instead, warning that the path is full of peril. With her arcane magic she sends those who accept to Jeziba in Andorhal.

title: Rivern Frostwind
body: Rivern Frostwind is a night elf who lives atop Frostsaber Rock with his companion Glacier, training the wild frostsabers of Winterspring to bear riders. He calls them the most feral and difficult to subdue of all the sabers, and he will sell one only to the most trusted, who must earn acceptance from him and from the cats alike. Those who would prove themselves begin humbly, gathering meat to feed the sabers in training, then drive the crazed Winterfall furbolgs from the rock and strike at the frostmaul giants in the name of Shy-Rotam. Discipline and determination, he says, are what he asks above all.

title: Witch Doctor Mau'ari
body: Witch Doctor Mau'ari is a jungle troll who has made a home among the goblins of Everlook and claims she always knows what a visitor has come for. From the reflective shards of the frostmaul giants she makes a lucky charm, the Cache of Mau'ari. Carried on the hunt, it lets its bearer capture e'ko, the spiritual power every creature holds, from the frostsabers, wildkin, yeti and other beasts of the valley. Mau'ari knows an incantation that turns e'ko into juju, and the charm's shining surface reflects that power onto whoever holds it: the speed of the frostsaber, or the keen mind of the wildkin.

title: Storm Shadowhoof
body: Storm Shadowhoof is a tauren who stands in Everlook and sets trials for those who wish to prove their worth. He sends them first against Ursius, a clever shardtooth bear of the northwestern hills who has made prey of every hunter sent after him, then against Brumeran, a graceful and deadly chimaera of the south. The last trial is the hardest: to gather sacred meat from the frostsabers and lay it at the stone of Shy-Rotam, calling the matriarch out in fury. Those who pass he sends with his marker to his friend Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff, so that their deeds are never forgotten.

title: Umi Rumplesnicker
body: Umi Rumplesnicker of Everlook has long felt that her friends' clever ideas outshine her own, and she is tired of their teasing about the ones she has. Her answer is a mechanical yeti, covered in thick fur and crowned with pristine horns taken from the Ice Thistle yeti, and meant to give her friends the fright of their lives: Legacki here in Everlook, Sprinkle in Gadgetzan and Quixxil at Marshal's Refuge in Un'Goro. Legacki jumps and shrieks, then guesses at once who is behind it, for Umi is forever playing jokes on Legacki. She is delighted, certain her friends will think twice before mocking her ideas again.

title: Umbranse the Spiritspeaker
body: Umbranse the Spiritspeaker is an aged human medium who lives in a small house in the snowy hills northeast of Everlook, sharing a camp with the Wintersaber Trainers. He speaks for the dead, and the green dragonflight counts him among its mortal allies: when Itharius sought a way to reach the dragon Eranikus, who lies between sleep and death, he sent his helpers to Umbranse. The old man agreed to lend his gift, though his most potent augury device had been taken from him against his will. He also gave the Argent Dawn in Everlook a book, Studies in Spirit Speaking, which its envoy found close to unreadable.

title: Earthcaller Franzahl
body: At the bottom of Darkwhisper Gorge, among the demons, waits Earthcaller Franzahl, a high elf who studies the known and unknown elements of the world. No mortal has spoken the word elementium to him in decades. His former student Krixix, a goblin, spent a lifetime trying to reach the chained gods of the underworld and what would form only where the elements clash. Nearly a decade ago Krixix opened a fissure in this very gorge, and an agent of Therazane sprang out of it. The two spoke, then the fissure closed and Krixix was gone, swallowed whole. Franzahl warns that what one wishes for may become what one does not want.

title: Lorax
body: Lorax is a satyr who paces the ruins of a night elf temple above Frostwhisper Gorge, talking to himself. Mock him as mad and he threatens to rip out your tongue; ask what he does and he answers that he broods, laments, hates and plots, then broods again. He dreams of catching Goraluk Anvilcrack. Lorax agreed to teach that Blackrock orc the secret of demon forging in exchange for his soul, a poor price, though in such times any soul is better than none. Goraluk ran off with the unforged, rune-covered breastplate without paying, and Lorax suspects he cowers in Blackrock Spire, trying to finish it without the knowledge only Lorax holds.

title: Artorius the Amiable
body: A tauren who calls himself Artorius the Amiable wanders the high north of Winterspring. He greets travelers warmly, delighted to meet another soul in so remote a corner of the world, and invites them to walk with him so that they may keep each other warm. The kindness is a mask. Artorius is a doomguard of the Burning Legion, one of the demonic corrupters that the ancient Vartrus of Felwood would see destroyed, and his true name is Artorius the Doombringer. Like the other agents of the Legion he flees from groups, yet turns to destroy any who face him alone.

title: The Winterfall Firewater
body: Meggi Peppinrocker of Everlook boasts of her golden hours in the wild, then remembers to send the willing on to Donova Snowden at the hot springs. The Winterfall furbolgs have grown fiercely protective of the larger pools, and an empty flask taken from one of them holds drops of a glowing green liquid. It reminds Donova of the sludge she saw in Felwood. Winterfall runners pass through Timbermaw Hold to the corrupted Deadwood tribe, and in a Deadwood cauldron bubbles the same foul goo, which Donova suspects is drawn from the toxic horrors of Irontree Woods. Mixed with the spring water, the poison loses its toxicity yet still affects whoever drinks it for a time: the Winterfall need the springs to purify their firewater. Their runners' shipments are seized, and High Chief Winterfall, whose orders seem to have set his once peaceful tribe raging, is slain. His crude log goes to Kelek Skykeeper of the Emerald Circle in Felwood, who promises to send word once he has read it.

title: Salfa's Watch
body: Salfa stands at the Winterspring gate of Timbermaw Hold, both speaker for the Timbermaw in this land and defender of the tribe. Nafien, who keeps the Felwood gate, sends the tribe's friends through the hold to Salfa, warning them to hurry and never to strike a Timbermaw, even in self defense. Salfa tells them that the Winterfall of this frozen land were once allies of the Timbermaw, until the strange demands of their high chief turned them on everything they met. Now they have fallen under the same corrupting sway as the Deadwood of Felwood, consumed by fear and hatred of all they do not understand. Salfa asks that their numbers be thinned, saddening as the task is, and gathers the spirit beads the Winterfall carry to ward off foul spirits, charms that plainly failed them. A ritual totem taken from them reeks of dread, and the Timbermaw within the hold study it, hoping that one day the Winterfall will rage against them no more.

title: The Crystal of Zin-Malor
body: Ivy Leafrunner in Felwood and Daryn Lightwind of Rut'theran Village send the curious to Wynd Nightchaser of Starfall Village, who knows the tale of Kel'Theril. The Highborne there stole a sacred relic to siphon its power, and it shattered beneath the frozen lake, cursing them to haunt the place forever. The dwarf Jaron Stoneshaper lends his pick to dig the fragments out of the ice and points the way to Aurora Skycaller near the Northpass Tower in the Eastern Plaguelands. Pained by the mistakes of her ancestors, she still names the shards: the Crystal of Zin-Malor, which can contain and control great arcane forces. With sacred writings from its temple in Azshara, an enchanted thorium bar, crystal restoratives and water from the dire pool of Dire Maul, she makes it whole. Carried back to the lake, the crystal stirs one remorseful spirit to call on its brethren to let go of the past. The crystal can never go home to its ruined temple, so Wynd sends it to Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus to be kept safe.

title: The Altar of Elune
body: Erelas Ambersky of Rut'theran Village found that wildkin feathers from the Hinterlands carry an inborn magic, and wondered whether the wildkin of Winterspring shared it. Moontouched feathers gathered from the snow proved that they did, and Erelas sent their finder on to his colleague Ranshalla below Owl Wing Thicket. With incantations copied from the Ruins of Kel'Theril, she climbs the ridge through the owlbeast caves, chanting while her companion lights the torches one by one, until the altar of Elune at the summit glows. Priestesses of the goddess appear and tell their tale. A gem there once let them speak with Elune herself, and to guard it the goddess gave them the wildkin, fierce protectors of all her sacred places. Without her guidance the wildkin have grown feral and confused, yet wherever they are found they still guard something of importance. Told of all this, Fandral Staghelm remarks only that the druids have long known it.

title: Wild Guardians
body: Trull Failbane of the Horde has heard that the wildkin of Winterspring guard secrets of the night elves, and he means to learn what they hide. His hunters push into the valley past the ragged owlbeasts south of the road and the raging owlbeasts of its center, then north among the moontouched owlbeasts, fiercer still, and at last to a series of small caves in the south, where berserk wildkin seem to have gone mad from the very thing they protect. From the neck of one slain wildkin falls a necklace of blue feathers that glows, fading slowly in and out. Trull knows the beasts but not their magic, and sends the necklace to Nara Wildmane in Thunder Bluff. Nara senses only one source in its light. The wildkin, she says, were made by the night elf goddess Elune to guard her most sacred places, and though they are confused now, they once had a purpose. She urges the bearer to look deeper.
